ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory CDD and EDD screening of all shareholders, UBOs, directors and authorized representatives against: (i) the State Bank of Vietnam PEP list; (ii) domestic security and law-enforcement blacklists maintained by the Ministry of Public Security; (iii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists implemented by Vietnamese authorities; (iv) OFAC SDN List and other US sanctions administered by the Department of the Treasury; and (v) EU and other international restrictive measures. Screening must occur at onboarding, before name clearance, before licensed incorporation, and continuously throughout the business relationship. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory where any subject is a PEP, a person resident or incorporated in a FATF-listed high-risk jurisdiction, or where the transaction is high-value, complex, or not transparently funded. The result of each screening must be documented and retained for at least five years under the AML Law and supporting decrees.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Business Registration Portal (NBRP) operated by the Agency for Business Registration under the Ministry of Planning and Investment – https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Articles 37–41 of the Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 and Article 14 of Decree No. 47/2021/NĐ-CP, every enterprise name must be written in the Vietnamese alphabet or in Vietnamese words with letters reproduced in Latin script; Roman numerals, other numerals and other symbols are permitted. The Vietnamese name must begin with one of the legal entity designators (Công ty TNHH, Công ty cổ phần, etc.), followed by the proper name. A foreign investor must transliterate its corporate name into a valid Vietnamese-language proper name for the enterprise; the foreign-language short name may be used in addition, but the registered Vietnamese name must be clear, lawful, not misleading, and not identical with or confusingly similar to another enterprise's name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name reservation is valid for 30 calendar days after provisional approval and is not extendable. If the NBRP or the provincial Department of Planning and Investment rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file a written administrative complaint with the same business registration office within the statutory time limit under the Law on Complaints No. 02/2011/QH13. The appeal must state the grounds of rejection, cite the exact name rule allegedly satisfied, and annex the original rejection notice. If the first-instance appeal is unsuccessful, the applicant may escalate to the Director of the Agency for Business Registration at the Ministry of Planning and Investment, or file an administrative litigation in a competent provincial court, while simultaneously submitting a new name proposal through the NBRP to avoid running out of the reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. A purely virtual address or mailbox without a physical, fixed and inspectable space is not acceptable for a licensed corporate secretarial and registered agent company. A serviced office lease may be used where the provider supplies a dedicated desk or meeting room, mail and courier handling, and access during business hours, and where the lease is evidenced by a signed contract and the address is included in the enterprise registration dossier.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 40% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the provincial Department of Planning and Investment or State Bank of Vietnam during the first operating year for an AML-supervised corporate secretarial provider; the likelihood rises to approximately 65% where a non-dedicated virtual office is detected or where the registered address is inconsistent with tax and business activity records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 (Articles 26, 27, 29, 38, 46-50, 110-120); Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14 (Articles 27-30, 36-38, 55-57); Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on Enterprise Registration (Articles 24-27, 41-48); Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP guiding the Law on Investment; Circular No. 01/2023/TT-BKHĐT on enterprise registration forms and procedures
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Agency for Business Registration, Ministry of Planning and Investment (MPI), and the Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) of the province/city where the head office is located; National Business Registration Portal (www.dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Investment Registration Certificate application (Form A-1/A-2 under Decree 31/2021/ND-CP) and Enterprise Registration Certificate application (Form I-5 under Circular No. 01/2023/TT-BKHĐT), submitted together with the statutory company dossier
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum charter capital applies to the non-conditional business line of registered agent/corporate secretarial services (ISIC 8299). Foreign investors subscribe charter capital in Vietnamese Dong or freely convertible currency and must fully contribute the committed capital within ninety (90) days from issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate, by wire transfer to the company's capital contribution account at a licensed bank. No escrow bank deposit is statutorily mandated, but the contribution schedule in the Investment Registration Certificate and Enterprise Registration Certificate must be strictly observed to avoid penalties, forced dissolution, or revocation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE MEMBERS COUNCIL
OF [COMPANY] LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY

Resolution No.: 01/[Year]/BM
Date: [Date]
Place: [Registered office address]

THE MEMBERS COUNCIL

Pursuant to the Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14, the Company Charter, and the Investment Registration Certificate No. [IRC No.] issued by [Provincial Department of Planning and Investment];

All members or authorized representatives of the members have unanimously adopted this resolution:

ARTICLE 1: SUBSCRIPTION OF CHARTER CAPITAL

The Charter Capital of the Company is [amount] VND, divided into [number] capital contribution portions among the members in accordance with the List of Members attached to this resolution. Each subscribing member irrevocably undertakes to contribute the amount set opposite its name, in freely convertible currency, in full within ninety (90) days after the Enterprise Registration Certificate is issued, by wire transfer to the Company capital contribution account or to the escrowed legal consultant account as directed by the competent authority. Any late contribution shall bear statutory interest.

ARTICLE 2: REGISTERED OFFICE AND FUNCTIONAL PREMISES

The Company hereby adopts [address] as its registered head office in Viet Nam. The head office shall be used for the Company records, statutory registration, service of process, registered agent services, and corporate secretarial operations. The General Director is instructed to execute the premises lease, obtain fire safety and environmental registrations, and secure all functional clearances.

ARTICLE 3: APPOINTMENT OF LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE AND OFFICERS

3.1. The Members Council appoints [full name and passport number of the appointed individual] as the Chairperson and legal representative of the Company, with authority to sign all contracts, finance documents, tax filings, and statutory registers. 3.2. The Members Council appoints [full name, passport number] as General Director, with day-to-day management powers as defined in the Company Charter. 3.3. The Members Council appoints [full name, tax qualification] as acting Chief Accountant responsible for statutory accounting and financial disclosure. 3.4. The legal representative is personally authorized to open bank accounts, register e-tax invoices, and deal with the State Bank of Vietnam.

ARTICLE 4: BANK ACCOUNTS AND CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION

The General Director is directed to open one or more capital contribution accounts and operating accounts at a licensed commercial bank in Viet Nam, to notify the bank of the Charter Capital schedule, and to comply with exchange control and foreign investment rules under the State Bank of Vietnam.

ARTICLE 5: COMMENCEMENT OF BUSINESS

The Company shall commence the licensed activities upon full satisfaction of all conditions under the Enterprise Registration Certificate, the Law on Investment, and applicable sectoral conditions. All officers are authorized to take all steps necessary for statutory incorporation and operation.

ARTICLE 6: EFFECTIVENESS

This Resolution is effective from the date of signing and shall remain valid until replaced by a subsequent resolution of the Members Council or shareholders meeting as applicable under the Law on Enterprises.

Signed by all members and witnesses: [signatures]

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal Structure Confirmation, Company Name Search and Premises Eligibility Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Business Registration Portal (NBRP) of the Agency for Business Registration – Ministry of Planning and Investment; online name search at dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a pre-filing screening of the proposed English and Vietnamese company names against the National Business Registration Portal database to ensure distinctiveness and legality under Article 38 of the Law on Enterprises. Verify applicable business lines against the conditional investment/business list under Decree 31/2021/ND-CP and confirm that ISIC 8299 corporate secretarial activity is non-conditional. Confirm the head-office address is eligible for lease, with lawful title or lease right that can be evidenced for the Enterprise Registration Dossier. Engage external legal counsel to prepare the Investment Registration Certificate and Enterprise Registration Certificate drafts. No application is filed at this step; the action is a mandatory due diligence gate.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name in Vietnamese and English (three alternatives)
Lease agreement or letter of intent for head office
Passport / legal entity status of foreign members and legal representatives
Decree 31/2021/ND-CP business-line checklist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts with an existing registered enterprise or with national historical/cultural names, resubmit using one of the alternative names or add distinctive characteristics (e.g., corporate identifiers) and re-check. If the address is queried, provide a new lease commitment letter and revise the dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Notarization and Legalization of Investment and Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Notary Office in Viet Nam; Department of Foreign Affairs/Consular section for overseas document legalization; certified translation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the company charter, list of members, members residential registration/passports, IRC application (Form A-1) and ERC application (Form I-5). Notarize the Vietnamese translations and copies of passports, certificate of incorporation of corporate investors, financial statements of the investor, and powers of attorney. If any document is issued abroad, it must be consular legalized or apostilled according to Vietnam's treaty obligations, and translated into Vietnamese by a licensed translation agent. The notarized copies will form part of the statutory submission package.
required_dossiers: Charter of the LLC
List of members
Application forms (IRC and ERC)
Passport copies and notarized translations
Investment capital commitment letter and financial evidence
Power of attorney appointing the signatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization is refused because of incomplete originals, remediate by producing originals or apostilled legalizations. If transfer of statutory capital from a corporate group triggers an outbound investment approval in the investor's home country, obtain that approval before re-submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission and Approval of Investment Registration Certificate (IRC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Registration Authority within Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) of the province where the head office is located; online through the National Investment Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete IRC application with DPI, either in person or online on the National Investment Portal. The proposal must describe the registered-agent and corporate-secretarial business, the investment project, scale, capital contribution schedule, and location. DPI shall coordinate with relevant provincial agencies and issue the IRC within 15 working days of the valid dossier (up to 10 additional days for projects under national security review). Thereafter, IRC approval automatically confirms the foreign investor's capital contribution entitlement for the registered scope.
required_dossiers: IRC application form (Form A-1/A-2 under Decree 31/2021/ND-CP)
Feasibility study / business plan for the service project
Lease agreement or land-use right document for the head office
Proof of financial capacity (bank confirmation, audited financial statements, or commitment)
Valid copies of investor's legal status and passport/identity papers
Power of attorney, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DPI issues a request for supplementation, respond fully within the statutory period (normally 10 working days) and re-submit. If the IRC is refused, file a complaint with the Agency for Foreign Investment under MPI or initiate administrative court proceedings within the statutory appeal window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC) / Business Registration Certificate Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office – Department of Planning and Investment (DPI); or online at National Business Registration Portal (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining IRC, submit to the DPI Business Registration Office an enterprise registration application dossier. DPI issues the ERC within 3 working days after receiving a complete and valid dossier. The ERC confirms the company's name, legal form, head-office address, business lines, charter capital, legal representatives, and members. Simultaneously, DPI will automatically register the enterprise's tax code and send the information to the tax authority.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Registration application (Form I-5)
Valid IRC copy
Company charter signed by members or their authorized representatives
List of members (Form II-1)
Valid ID / passport / legal status of legal representative (Form I-8)
Lease agreement and owner's valid real estate title for head office
Power of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On rejection due to non-compliant dossier, correct and supplement the dossier and resubmit; DPI must notify deficiencies in writing. Appeals lie to MPI and administrative court. During correction, the company may not commence operations until ERC is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Seal Registration and Seal Sample Notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Planning and Investment / National Business Registration Portal; licensed seal engraving service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the ERC is issued, engrave the corporate seal of the company with the seal sample conforming to Law on Enterprises Article 43 and Decree 01/2021/ND-CP. Immediately submit a seal-sample notification via the National Business Registration Portal (Form II-2). DPI shall publish the seal sample in the national database. The seal does not need a separate certificate but must be described precisely with the company name and enterprise registration code.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Registration Certificate
Seal sample notification form
Copy of legal representative's ID/passport
Seal engraving invoice/description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notification is rejected because the seal contains irregular Vietnamese characters or is not aligned with ERC data, re-engrave the seal and resubmit. Obtain DPI confirmation by the next working day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Bank Account Opening and Charter Capital Contribution Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Department of Taxation (tax code via DPI); licensed commercial bank in Viet Nam; State Bank of Vietnam for foreign exchange matters
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: With the ERC and tax code, the company shall complete tax-registration formalities, open a capital contribution account and operating account at a licensed bank. Foreign members shall transfer contributed capital in freely convertible currency before the statutory deadline (90 days from ERC). The legal representative files the capital-contribution notice and obtains an account confirmation. Register for electronic invoices with the tax authority and apply for a value-added tax code. For foreign invested services, submit foreign loan/supplier registration if applicable.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Registration Certificate
Investment Registration Certificate
Corporate charter and seal
Resolution of the Members Council opening bank accounts
Capital contribution schedule and bank confirmation
Legal representative ID/passport and residence card
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening because of KYC gaps, supplement corporate documents and provide beneficial ownership information. If capital contribution is late, remit interest and penalties; DPI may record the breach and enforce the project schedule. Correct contribution via wire transfer and evidence to bank/DPI.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial / Physical and Environmental License Clearances (Fire Safety, Environmental Registration, Occupational Clearance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Fire Prevention and Rescue Police; Department of Natural Resources and Environment (DONRE); Department of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prior to physical operation, submit the premises for fire safety design appraisal and fire safety acceptance testing under Law on Fire Prevention and Rescue and Decree 136/2020/ND-CP. Simultaneously, submit an environmental registration dossier for office / non-industrial service operations to DONRE based on waste generation thresholds. Obtain an environmental registration confirmation and occupational health and safety declaration. For office services, no industrial environmental permit (EPE) or full EIA is required; only Category III environmental registration if the premises release domestic wastewater and general solid waste.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or ownership proof of premises
Fire safety dossier: design documents, fire protection equipment layout, evacuation plan, and engineered construction drawings
Environmental registration form (Form 01 / 02 under Decree 08/2022/ND-CP)
Waste-water discharge or municipal sewer connection agreement
Occupational health and safety plan and workplace environmental monitoring reports
Structural load / building condition certificate from a licensed authority, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If fire safety approval is refused, remediate deficiencies (installation of extinguishers, exit signage, alarm, suppression systems) and re-submit. If environmental registration is incomplete, supplement an environmental monitoring report and operational data. The company cannot lawfully operate until the clearances are confirmed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Natural Resources and Environment (DONRE) – Provincial Environmental Management Division, and Provincial Fire Prevention and Rescue Police Department
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Environmental Registration Certificate (under Law on Environmental Protection 2020 and Decree 08/2022/ND-CP) and Fire Safety Acceptance Certificate (under Decree 136/2020/ND-CP)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MONRE) / Provincial Department of Natural Resources and Environment (DONRE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Category III under Decree 08/2022/ND-CP) – Full EIA not required; office-based registered agent and corporate secretarial service with no production activity, only minimal domestic wastewater and general solid waste
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Domestic wastewater discharged to municipal sewer must comply with QCVN 14:2008/BTNMT (domestic wastewater), or QCVN 01:2021/BXD (clean water) if local infrastructure requires; where there is no municipal sewer, on-site treatment must meet QCVN 14:2008/BTNMT. VOC-generating operations are not material; use of office printers and cleaning agents remains below exemptions under QCVN 05:2020/BTNMT (ambient air) and QCVN 20:2009/BTNMT (industrial emissions). Solid waste must be classified, stored, and transferred to a licensed waste contractor under the Law on Environmental Protection 2020, with waste-transfer records retained for at least three years. Noise and vibration at the workplace boundary must comply with QCVN 26:2010/BTNMT and QCVN 27:2010/BTNMT.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Design Appraisal and Acceptance Certificate by the Provincial Fire Prevention and Rescue Police under Decree 136/2020/ND-CP; the premises must comply with QCVN 06:2021/BXD for fire safety in buildings, including means of escape, fire alarm, extinguishers, and structural integrity. Civil defense requirements under Law on Civil Defense No. 02/2023/QH14 require the business to prepare an evacuation plan, assembly point, and emergency coordination with local authorities. Occupational clearance under Law on Occupational Safety and Health No. 84/2015/QH14 and Decree 44/2016/ND-CP requires registration of the occupational safety and health statement with the Department of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs, and compliance with workplace hygiene standards, including lighting (QCVN 22:2016/BYT), microclimate (QCVN 26:2016/BYT), noise and vibration (QCVN 27:2016/BYT), and structural load certification by a licensed engineering unit for multi-storey premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation (Tong Cuc Thue), Ministry of Finance of the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam; official national tax portal https://www.gdt.gov.vn; electronic filing and e-tax administration portal https://thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn; electronic invoice clearing portal https://hoadon.gdt.gov.vn; business registry integration through the National Business Registration Portal https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-invested Limited Liability Company: Step 1 - Obtain an Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) from the Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) under the Law on Investment 2020; Step 2 - Apply for an Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC) via the National Business Registration Portal; the DPI electronically transmits enterprise registration data to the tax authority; Step 3 - The General Department of Taxation automatically issues the statutory 10-digit Tax Identification Number (Ma so thue, MST) contemporaneously with ERC issuance, requiring no separate paper application from the foreign entity; Step 4 - Activate the e-tax account at https://thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn and register electronic invoice templates with the tax authority; Step 5 - Submit the initial registration dossier for taxes (Form 07-MST on the e-tax portal) covering VAT, CIT, and license fees; Step 6 - File the first provisional VAT/CIT declarations in accordance with Circular 80/2021/TT-BTC within the statutory filing calendar; foreign contractors without a Vietnamese establishment that derive Vietnam-source income must separately obtain an MST under the Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) regime through withholding procedures.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (resident Vietnamese enterprise subject to Corporate Income Tax on worldwide income at the headline 20% rate; no pass-through eligibility under Vietnamese law); global territorial scope for resident LLCs contrasted with territorial sourcing rules applicable to non-resident foreign contractors under the Foreign Contractor Tax regime; the registered agent and offshore secretarial business model is taxable as ordinary service income at CIT rates with no special tax-exempt-zone status unless physically located in an approved special economic zone or high-tech park under Decree 82/2018/ND-CP and applicable incentive schedules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Viet Nam has no US-style check-the-box or general hybrid mismatch election. Available statutory elections include: (a) election of VAT calculation method - credit (deduction) method versus direct method on added value - permitted for enterprises with annual revenue below VND 1 billion or with incomplete accounting records; (b) election of CIT incentive statuses under tax incentive roadmaps for eligible sectors and regions, including software production and high-technology industries subject to reduced 10% or 15% rates with tax holidays; (c) election of the small- and medium-sized enterprise accounting regime under Circular 132/2018/TT-BTC; (d) election of consolidated VAT offsetting (bu tru) among dependent branches; (e) election to create an offshore stable establishment or contract structure triggering Foreign Contractor Tax withholding obligations rather than full VAT registration in certain cross-border service supply scenarios; (f) anti-hybrid and substance rules under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP disallow deductions for payments designed to achieve double non-taxation or mismatches lacking economic substance, and no domestic election may override transfer-pricing documentation requirements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT, Thue Gia Tri Gia Tang) regulated by the Law on Value Added Tax No. 13/2008/QH12 as amended in 2013 and 2016, implementing Circular 219/2013/TT-BTC, Decree 209/2013/ND-CP, Decree 123/2020/ND-CP on e-invoices, and Tax Administration Law No. 38/2019/QH14; non-resident service providers are further exposed to Foreign Contractor Tax combining VAT and CIT on Vietnam-sourced service income.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VND 1,000,000,000 (VND one billion) annual revenue from sales of goods and services represents the statutory threshold governing the mandatory use of the full credit (deduction) method of VAT accounting; enterprises below this threshold may elect the direct method on a percentage-of-turnover basis. Micro-business households and individuals with annual taxable revenue not exceeding VND 100,000,000 are exempt from VAT registration. There is no general de minimis VAT registration exemption for a licensed LLC; once an enterprise registration exists, VAT registration and periodic filing obligations attach regardless of turnover, and zero-rated or exempt supplies must still be declared through the e-tax portal.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (Hoa Don Dien Tu) applies to all enterprises since 1 July 2022. Invoices must be created in the standardized XML format, digitally signed with a valid e-signature, and transmitted via a General Department of Taxation accredited e-invoice service provider to the national invoice portal (hoadon.gdt.govt.vn). The tax authority performs near-real-time fiscal clearance by assigning a unique tax-authority code (ma cua co quan thue) to each invoice bearing a mandatory QR code; web-service API integration (SOAP/REST XML) with the central exchange system is required for high-volume issuers. The QR code must encode the tax authority code, seller tax ID, total amount, and invoice date. Real-time clearance is obligatory before the invoice is legally valid for the buyer's input VAT credit; foreign-invested LLCs must also report e-invoice summaries in the periodic e-filing cycle.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0%) applies to exported goods and to services supplied to foreign organizations or foreign individuals that are consumed entirely outside Viet Nam, under Article 9 of Circular 219/2013/TT-BTC. For the registered agent and offshore secretarial services business, eligibility requires all of the following conditions: (a) the service recipient is a non-resident organization without a permanent establishment in Viet Nam; (b) the service is physically performed and delivered for use outside Viet Nam, meaning off-shore corporate secretarial deliverables, registry administration, and statutory filing outputs are deemed consumed in the foreign recipient's jurisdiction; (c) payment is received through a licensed Vietnamese bank in a convertible foreign currency with an inward remittance certificate or matching bank SWIFT statement; (d) the services are not listed on the prohibited domestic consumption services list, which includes real estate intermediation, insurance, financial derivatives, and postal/telecommunications services with a domestic consumption nexus; and (e) complete documentation substantiates the offshore nature of consumption and the actual delivery of secretarial work outside Viet Nam. If the foreign service recipient is deemed to have a Vietnamese permanent establishment, or if the service is rendered through a domestic delivery channel, the zero rate is denied and standard 10% VAT applies. The LLC must separately declare zero-rated revenue on the VAT return and retain full audit trails for input VAT refund claims on exported service costs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (To Khai Hai Quan) authenticated by the customs electronic clearance system and stamped discharge record for physical goods; for services, the equivalent export declaration is replaced by the service contract and GDT-accepted proof of offshore consumption
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing shipment from Vietnam and arrival in the foreign destination (for goods exports only)

Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a licensed Vietnamese bank or a detailed bank statement evidencing receipt of foreign currency from the foreign service recipient within the statutory repatriation period

Export service contract in English or Vietnamese between the VN LLC and the non-resident client, accompanied by a signed service-delivery acceptance certificate (Bien Ban Nghiem Thu) evidencing offshore performance
Foreign client's certificate of incorporation or valid business registration certificate from the foreign jurisdiction, plus documentation of the foreign party's tax residence status
E-invoice with tax authority code showing zero-rated supplies and the corresponding standard-value invoice issued under the Foreign Trade Exchange contract

Workpapers demonstrating the offshore consumption of registered agent and corporate secretarial services, including email correspondence, deliverable acceptance logs, and foreign regulatory filings evidencing the service utility
Declaration of export service performance under Circular 80/2021/TT-BTC detailing the shipment, service, and foreign-currency proceeds attributable to the zero-rated transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Viet Nam's tax authority conducts post-clearance audits comparing export declarations, service contracts, and inward remittances. If zero-rating cannot be substantiated with the mandatory documentation bundle, the tax authority reclassifies the revenue as domestic taxable supply and imposes: (a) additional VAT at 10% or the temporary reduced rate, plus late-payment interest at 0.03% per day computed from the original filing due date; (b) administrative penalties under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP - for underdeclaration exceeding 10% of the correct liability, a penalty of up to 20% of the underpaid tax; for deliberate tax evasion or fraudulently claiming zero-rating, a penalty of one to three times the evaded amount; (c) retrospective clawback of any input VAT refunds previously granted in respect of zero-rated export transactions, together with statutory interest; (d) suspension of e-invoice issuance privileges and potential revocation of the enterprise's license for severe violations; (e) criminal liability under Article 200 of the Penal Code (Law No. 100/2015/QH13), imposing fines up to VND 4.5 billion and imprisonment up to seven years for tax evasion involving VND 100 million or more; (f) for failure to repatriate foreign-currency export proceeds within 180 days without lawful extension, the State Bank of Viet Nam may impose monetary sanctions under Decree 88/2019/ND-CP of up to VND 500 million for foreign-exchange ordinance violations; and (g) the audit limitation period is 10 years for tax fraud and 5 years for other violations pursuant to Law on Tax Administration No. 38/2019/QH14, providing a long window for retrospective clawbacks and reassessment of fraudulent zero-rating claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (SBV - Ngan Hang Nha Nuoc Viet Nam), specifically the Foreign Exchange Administration Department and the Banking Supervision Agency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Vietnamese Dong (VND) is a managed-float currency and is not freely convertible. Current-account transactions, including cross-border service fees receivable from offshore clients for registered-agent and secretarial work, are generally convertible through SBV-licensed credit institutions, subject to production of the underlying service agreement, tax invoice, and corporate income tax compliance. Capital-account transactions (charter capital contribution, shareholder loans, equity transfers, and foreign borrowings) require prior investment registration with the Ministry of Planning and Investment and must be effected through a Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) opened at an authorized bank. Profit remittance to foreign shareholders is a current-account-like flow but is permitted only after the annual CIT finalization, audited financial statements, and satisfaction of the profit-remittance documentation requirements under Circular No. 186/2010/TT-BTC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Ordinance on Foreign Exchange No. 06/2005/PL-UBTVQH11 and its implementing regulations, the VN LLC, as an exporter of services, must repatriate all export proceeds to Vietnam within 180 days from the completion of service delivery and invoice issuance, crediting the amounts to a foreign-currency account at an SBV-licensed bank. The current mandatory conversion ratio is 0% for lawful export receipts; the SBV, however, retains the statutory power to require temporary mandatory sale of foreign currency to authorized banks during periods of exchange-rate stress. Retained foreign currency must remain in the licensed foreign-currency account and cannot be held abroad without SBV permission.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Foreign Trade of Vietnam (Vietcombank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: DICA / USD Foreign-Currency Current Account / VND Operating Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank for Investment and Development of Vietnam JSC (BIDV)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: DICA / USD Foreign-Currency Account / VND Operating Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Vietnam Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Industry and Trade (VietinBank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: DICA / USD Foreign-Currency Account / VND Operating Account

USD Foreign-Currency Account / VND Operating Account / Import-Export Trade Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium. Vietnam does not recognize offshore digital EMIs under Decree No. 101/2012/ND-CP (as amended) governing non-cash payments; payment-intermediary services require an SBV license, which offshore EMIs do not hold. Consequently, an offshore EMI cannot open a VND settlement account, issue domestic IBANs, or clear payments into Vietnam as a principal. Such platforms may be used only as a supplementary inbound collection channel for small-ticket client fees, with the final leg landing in the VN LLC's licensed-bank account through the EMI's local partner bank. Their use does not reduce statutory AML/KYC obligations, and the authoritative treasury ledger, tax invoice trail, and FX records must always be maintained within Vietnam.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is required. For a foreign-invested LLC in the Medium-Risk Enhanced category, Tier-1 domestic banks generally require the legal representative or a Vietnamese-resident authorized director (holding a notarized and consular-legalized power of attorney with Vietnamese translation) to appear in person at the branch for the KYC interview. Fully remote/eKYC account opening is not available for FDI entities. The standard onboarding bundle includes the original Enterprise Registration Certificate, Investment Registration Certificate, charter, board resolution on account opening and signatory authority, passports of all UBOs, and an AML beneficial-ownership self-declaration. A videoconference interview may be tolerated only after the local authorized officer physically presents the complete documentation set.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner opacity through offshore jurisdictions (e.g., BVI, Samoa) in the ownership chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and legalized corporate ownership tree from the ultimate individual to the VN LLC; UBO declaration matching SBV Circular No. 09/2023/TT-NHNN content; certified passports of all natural-person owners; certificate of good standing and register-of-directors extract for each intermediate entity; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements with supporting bank records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business description as 'registered agent / offshore secretarial' raising nominee-management or anonymity risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory register of controllers maintained at the registered office; executed client engagement letters and master service agreements naming the ultimate clients; detailed service-delivery evidence and time records; AML/CFT policy and client due-diligence files of the VN LLC; written confirmation that no nominee shareholding, bearer shares, or bearer warrants exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: All directors and signatories are non-residents, or a signatory holds PEP status.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Appointment of a Vietnamese-resident compliance officer with an employment contract; PEP self-certification for all shareholders and signatories; enhanced-due-diligence narrative memorandum; temporary-residence cards or valid business visas of directors; bank's internal beneficial-owner checklist countersigned by the resident officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Projected fee income and transaction velocity materially inconsistent with stated charter capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month cash-flow forecast; executed master service agreements with customer names (or a bank-accepted anonymized structure); issued invoices and collection aging summary; CIT provisional filings and tax payment receipts; bank statements of the foreign parent or shareholder demonstrating legitimate commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border pass-through pattern: funds received from overseas clients and promptly disbursed to overseas subcontractors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contract chain evidencing the principal-agent service model; subcontractor agreements and invoices; Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) returns and payment vouchers; value-added explanation memorandum; signed undertaking that the VN LLC does not operate a payment corridor for third parties and that all domestic taxes are settled from the Vietnamese account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: After the issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate and Investment Registration Certificate, the VN LLC opens a Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) at the chosen licensed bank. Charter-capital and shareholder-loan remittances are made via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign investor's own bank account (name and legal identity must match the investment registration), using the SBV-prescribed purpose code for direct investment capital contribution and a narrative referencing the ERC and IRC numbers. The receiving bank verifies the wire against the capital-contribution schedule, credits the DICA in foreign currency, and files the transaction with the SBV Foreign Exchange Administration. Conversion into VND is allowed only for lawful operating expenses within the registered business scope, supported by underlying invoices and payment requests.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational cross-border payments (service imports, software subscriptions, subcontractor fees, royalties) are executed via SWIFT MT103 priority transfers from the VN LLC's USD or VND account through the licensed bank; the bank requires the underlying commercial contract, tax invoice, and Foreign Contractor Tax confirmation. For physical goods procurements, Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) and documentary collections are available through the bank's trade desk subject to import declarations and customs documentation. Profit and dividend remittances follow Circular No. 186/2010/TT-BTC: audited financial statements, CIT finalization proof, board resolution, and bank confirmation, then executed via MT103 with the SBV purpose code for profit remittance. All outbound wires must carry the correct purpose code and be supported by a fully documented commercial rationale.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable USD/VND forward contracts with an SBV-licensed credit institution (typical tenor up to 365 days, requiring genuine underlying commercial exposure).
Cross-currency swaps (USD/VND and USD/other major currencies) executed with a licensed bank for hedging committed cash flows.
Vanilla FX options (call/put on USD/VND) purchased from a licensed bank for hedging real transaction exposures; option writing by non-bank entities is not permissible.
Natural hedging through simultaneous USD-denominated receivables and payables, using the authorized foreign-currency current account without a derivative instrument.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for domestic residents; residents may not participate in the offshore VND NDF market without SBV authorization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business License Tax ('Lệ phí môn bài') – Enterprise License Fee Declaration and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Department of Taxation via the National E-Tax Portal (etaxvn.gov.vn)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Existing limited liability companies: by 30 January of each fiscal year; newly established LLCs are exempt for the year of incorporation and pay from the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 0.03% per day on the unpaid fee; administrative fines for late filing up to VND 25,000,000; repeated non-payment may lead to forced collection, suspension of tax invoice usage, and coordination with the Provincial Department of Planning and Investment for enterprise-registration sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements for the Foreign-Invested LLC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Department of Taxation, Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI), and General Statistics Office of Vietnam
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days from the end of the fiscal year (calendar-year companies: on or before 31 March)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-submission fines between VND 5,000,000 and VND 25,000,000 under the Tax Administration Law; inaccurate or unaudited statements may be rejected, trigger a tax-examination or reassessment, and expose the legal representative to administrative penalties; continued non-compliance may be recorded in the enterprise compliance file and used by DPI in enterprise-registration revocation proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Finalization Return and Payment Package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Department of Taxation via the National E-Tax Portal (provincial tax jurisdiction of the LLC's registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 March immediately following the calendar tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing administrative fine up to VND 25,000,000; late-payment interest at 0.03% per day on outstanding CIT arrears; serious or repeated violations can result in forced tax collection, temporary suspension of VAT invoices, and referral to DPI for corporate-registration sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All foreign-invested limited liability companies, irrespective of revenue, turnover, headcount, or asset size, must obtain a statutory independent audit of their annual financial statements under Vietnam's Law on Independent Audit; there is no de minimis exemption for the LLC's corporate secretarial scope.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnamese Accounting Standards (VAS), issued pursuant to the Law on Accounting, with presentation in Vietnam Dong (VND); IFRS is permitted only for consolidated financial statements of qualifying ultimate parents under Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Vietnam does not impose an annual UBO confirmation filing for ordinary LLCs. Beneficial-owner data is captured at registration and must be updated through the National Business Registration Portal within 10 working days after any change in member equity, shareholding transfers, or appointing a new legal representative. The LLC must maintain an up-to-date internal UBO/AML compliance file and disclose UBO details to licensed banks, tax authorities, and the registered agent upon lawful request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and Equity Transfer Ledger
Minute Book of Member Meetings and Resolutions
Register of Legal Representatives and Senior Executives

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 – USD 1,000 per year for professional registered-agent, company secretarial, and registered-address services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 600 – USD 2,500 per year for a statutory independent audit of a small to mid-sized foreign-invested LLC with limited transactions

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard rate 20%; no statutory tax holiday or preferential rate is specifically available for corporate secretarial / registered agent services (ISIC 8299). Targeted incentives (e.g., 10% rate for 15 years, 4-year exemption plus 9-year 50% reduction) apply exclusively to qualifying high-tech, high-technology support industries, and certain incentivised sectors, which are not ordinary service activities. Foreign-invested economic organizations may enjoy incentives only if the project meets the investment eligibility list under Law on Investment 2020 and Decree 31/2021/ND-CP.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly Provisional CIT Return – Form 02/TNDN; filed electronically through the General Department of Taxation (GDT) e-Tax portal at https://etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn. Payment and declaration can also be submitted via licensed tax service providers, but the e-Tax filing obligation applies to all enterprises.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than the last day of the first month following the end of each calendar quarter (for a standard calendar-year company: Q1 – 30 April, Q2 – 31 July, Q3 – 31 October, Q4 – 31 January of the following year). A company with an approved different fiscal year uses the equivalent quarter-end deadlines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enterprise identification: name, tax identification number (MST), and address as registered in the Enterprise Registration Certificate / Investment Registration Certificate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Vietnamese LLC must use its own Vietnamese MST. Do not insert the foreign parent or offshore shareholder’s tax ID. The foreign investor is not a CIT filer at the company level.
Foreign-invested LLCs default to a calendar year unless the Ministry of Finance has approved a different annual accounting period; the approved period must be stated consistently.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue in VND arising in the quarter, including revenue from corporate secretarial and registered agent services supplied to offshore clients.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Consolidate all Vietnamese-source and export revenue; foreign currency receipts must be converted to VND at the actual exchange rate as prescribed by the State Bank of Vietnam.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: actual expenses directly incurred for the business with valid invoices and vouchers, limited to the CIT deductibility rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to overseas affiliates must satisfy the arm's length rule and be documented; otherwise, they will be disallowed when calculating taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income: revenue minus deductible expenses plus other taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The company must allocate revenue and expenses correctly; inbound/outbound related-party transactions must be reported on the TP declaration schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carried forward deduction: taxable losses from prior years offset against current-year profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses may be carried forward for up to 5 consecutive years; no carryback is permitted. The offset schedule must be attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT rate: 20% standard; special preferential rate (e.g., 10%, 15%) only if applicant holds a valid preferential certificate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a secretarial/registered agent service company, use 20%. If a preferential rate was wrongly applied, the tax authority will reassess and impose penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisional CIT payable: current-quarter tax attributable after applying quarterly estimated calculation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Underpaid quarterly provisional amounts are subject to interest penalties at the statutory rate (0.03% per day). Overpayments are credited at the annual finalisation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late submission of a quarterly CIT return triggers an administrative fine under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP, ranging from VND 10,000,000 to VND 25,000,000 if the return is not filed within 90 days after the deadline; a late return filed earlier attracts lower fines (up to VND 8,000,000). The underpaid tax amount accrues interest at 0.03% per day from the statutory due date to the actual payment date. Failure to file may also lead to a tax assessment based on available records and a sanction for failure to provide information.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Final CIT Return (Quyet toan thue TNDN) – Form 03/TNDN; filed via the same GDT e-Tax portal or approved e-filing software; accompanying schedules (e.g., Form 01-1/TNDN, Form 01-2/TNDN, Form 01-3/TNDN) must be attached where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 90 days from the end of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year company, no later than 31 March of the following year. A foreign-invested LLC with an approved different fiscal year must file within 90 days after that fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enterprise identification: name, tax code, address, legal representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Legal representative of the Vietnamese LLC must be a natural person. If the global chief executive officer (or equivalent) is an offshore individual, that person is not automatically required to sign the Vietnamese tax return; the Vietnamese director or authorised representative must sign and bear responsibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue from operations (Doanh thu): all revenue from sales and services, including offshore secretarial and registered agent fees invoiced to foreign clients.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not report non-taxable income (e.g., loans received, capital contributions) in this line; otherwise the turnover base is distorted and penalties may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: total actual expenses attributable to generating the revenue, supported by invoices and lawful accounting documents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses incurred for offshore services without VAT invoices are still deductible if they are supported by contractual documents and paid via cross-border wire, provided the CIT deductibility conditions are met and the amounts are reasonable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Other taxable income: dividends from domestic companies (if any), gains on disposal of assets, interest income, foreign exchange gains, etc.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a registered agent/secretarial company, this is normally negligible; but examine all bank interest and foreign currency revaluations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Comprehensive taxable income before loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add the result of Line 2 minus Line 3 plus Line 4; any non-deductible expenses must be added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Less: tax loss carryforward of previous years (maximum 5 consecutive years per tax period).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a foreign-invested LLC may offset future profits only if the enterprise maintains adequate books and records; a reorganisation might break continuity.
This amount is the basis for applying the CIT rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT payable: taxable income multiplied by 20% (or applicable preferential rate).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-invested LLCs engaged in non-export service activities generally pay 20%. The tax authority will not recognise a preferential rate absent an explicit approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly provisional CIT already paid during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Subtract the sum of quarterly payments. If the provisional payments were less than 80% of the actual final CIT, a fine of 20% of the underpaid amount applies; interest also starts from the due date of the finalisation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additional CIT payable or overpayment to be refunded/offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If additional tax is payable, remit it no later than the finalisation deadline; refund claims for overpayments must be made through the e-Tax portal and may be subject to desk audits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual CIT finalisation within 90 days leads to a fine of up to VND 25,000,000 under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP, plus a daily interest charge of 0.03% on the outstanding tax. If the finalisation shows additional tax underpaid, the company also incurs an administrative penalty equal to 20% of the underpaid amount (unless the company timely amended before detection). Directors can be personally named in penalty decisions for false certification of the return.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (no dividend withholding tax on corporate shareholders). Under Vietnamese domestic law, after-tax profits remitted to a foreign corporate shareholder are not subject to an additional dividend WHT, provided the company has fully satisfied its CIT obligations. For a foreign individual shareholder, a final personal income tax withholding of 5% applies to cash dividends under the PIT law.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because domestic Vietnam imposes no dividend WHT, treaty relief is generally not required for ordinary dividends paid by a Vietnamese LLC to a foreign corporate shareholder. For payments that are subject to withholding (e.g., royalties or interest), the payer/recipient seeking treaty protection must submit a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the non-resident shareholder jurisdiction of residence to the Vietnamese tax authority before or at the time the payment is made. The procedure involves filing a written notification (using GDT’s form for Treaty Relief and accompanying documents) together with the withholding return, explaining the entitlement and computing the reduced rate. The tax office may request a certificate of beneficial ownership and evidence of the recipient's economic substance in the treaty country. If the relief is granted administratively, the excess withholding is refunded or creditable; unaided reliance on a treaty in the tax return is not recognised unless the procedure has been completed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties (IP license fees): statutory Foreign Contractor CIT rate is 10% on gross royalty, plus VAT at 5% where applicable (effective VAT on royalties is 5% on the payment; the net VAT burden varies). Under Vietnamese DTAs, royalty CIT may be reduced, typically to 5%, 10% or 15%, depending on the treaty partner and category of IP. Interest paid to a foreign lender: statutory Foreign Contractor CIT rate is 5% on gross interest; VAT is not charged on interest. Many Vietnam DTAs reduce interest WHT to a range of 5% to 10% (some treaties exempt interest entirely), subject to submission of the lender’s TRC and a statement that the lender is the beneficial owner and is not a nominal conduit.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP, a taxpayer is exempt from preparing the TP documentation (Local File and Master File) if: (i) the enterprise's total revenue in the fiscal year is less than VND 50 billion and the total value of all related-party transactions (including loans) is less than VND 30 billion; or (ii) the enterprise operates under a 'low-risk' status and meets the simplified declaration conditions. If total revenue equals or exceeds VND 50 billion, or related-party transactions equal or exceed VND 30 billion, the Vietnamese entity must prepare a Local File. A Master File is required when its ultimate parent company has consolidated global revenue of at least VND 20 trillion in the prior fiscal year. Even when documentation is exempt, the enterprise must still declare related-party transactions on the annual CIT finalisation form (Form 03/TNDN, Appendix) and maintain contemporaneous evidence of arm's length pricing.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vietnam does not operate a statutory Economic Substance Regulations regime (ESR) akin to the UAE or Cayman Islands. However, the Law on Tax Administration No. 38/2019/QH14 and Decree 132/2020/ND-CP incorporate a thorough substance-over-form doctrine and general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR): the tax authority may recharacterise transactions, disregard any arrangement lacking real economic substance, and reassess tax based on the actual commercial substance. A Vietnamese LLC providing registered agent/offshore secretarial services without maintaining local employees, office equipment, management decisions or commercial functions in Vietnam – or which simply routes fees to an offshore shell – risks being treated as a sham entity; its income may be deemed attributable to the foreign shareholder or a permanent establishment, and the CIT reassessment will be accompanied by penalties and interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting or lowering revenue derived from offshore registered agent and company secretarial services in CIT returns; generating fake invoices or entering fictitious expenses to reduce taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil: repayment of evaded tax plus interest of 0.03% per day; an administrative fine of up to 4 times the understated tax amount under the Law on Tax Administration 2019. Criminal: if the amount evaded is VND 100 million or more, prosecution under Article 200 of the Penal Code (ss. 1-4) with fines up to VND 4.5 billion and/or imprisonment of 3 to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative or director who signs the CIT return is personally liable alongside the company for the evaded tax and penalty; is subject to a travel ban (no exit visa) and a management ban; and in criminal cases may be sentenced to imprisonment of up to 7 years, with confiscation of assets and civil restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed / unregistered operation of corporate secretarial and registered agent services
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing regulated corporate secretarial, commercial agency, or registered office services without a valid Enterprise Registration Certificate or without the required investment registration for the foreign-invested LLC; or continuing operations after suspension/revocation of the licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative sanction under Decree 122/2021/ND-CP and the Law on Enterprises 2020: fine ranging from VND 80,000,000 to VND 100,000,000 for operating without a licence or after licence revocation; additional fine possible for undeclared foreign ownership; compulsory suspension of the business and forced dissolution of the Vietnamese entity; any contracts entered into during the unauthorised period may be declared void.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly liable for any civil loss suffered by clients or third parties from the invalid contracts; they may be subject to administrative fines in their personal capacity (up to VND 50,000,000); in cases involving fraud or misrepresentation, criminal liability under Articles 217 or 221 of the Penal Code (false trading / wrongful business) with imprisonment of up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registered agent and offshore secretarial activities are used to form or manage shell clients without performing customer due diligence, beneficial ownership checks, or submitting suspicious transaction reports to the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV); deliberately acting as a front for illicit shell companies or financial crime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering Law 2022, Decree 125/2020 and SBV Circular 11/2023/TT-NHNN: administrative fine up to VND 500,000,000 for serious non-compliance; revocation of operating licence; permanent suspension of the business; if the conduct is linked to money laundering, criminal sanctions under Article 324 of the Penal Code with fines and imprisonment of up to 10 years for repeat offenders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally accountable for AML compliance deficiencies; they can be fined personally, subject to travel bans and a prohibition from holding management positions; where they knew or should have known of the laundering scheme, imprisonment for money laundering ranges from 3 to 10 years, and they are jointly liable civilly for clients' and the State's recoveries.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing manipulation / lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging artificially high management fees to the Vietnamese entity from a related offshore registered agent, or shifting profits from Vietnam to a low-tax jurisdiction through non-arm's length secretarial fees; maintaining only a 'brass plate' office with no real economic functions, personnel, or risk assumption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP, the tax authority will recompute the taxpayer's income using the arm's length standard, disallow the excess related-party deductions, and impose additional CIT at 20%; late payment interest accrues at 0.03% per day; an administrative penalty of 20% of the underpaid tax applies for incorrect transfer pricing declarations, escalating to criminal tax evasion if the mispricing is fraudulent and exceeds the criminal threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who certified the TP documentation and final CIT return may be jointly liable for the additional tax and interest; a serious, deliberate transfer pricing fraud can expose directors to criminal liability under Article 200 of the Penal Code including imprisonment of up to 7 years and a travel ban; the company may be disqualified from obtaining certain tax and customs incentives in the future.
